item.description:
Platform: Splunk


Release Notes:

bug fixes


Description:
Synack helps organizations with the full spectrum of their security testing needs. We harness the world’s most exclusive team of security researchers and give them access to a powerful platform for trusted security testing. That testing yields vulnerabilities, data to measure attack surfaces, and provides documentation to aid compliance. The Synack App for Splunk provides an easy way to bring live, up-to-date Synack data into your Splunk environment. By putting IT, Security, and Synack-discovered vulnerability data in one place, richer reporting, analytics, custom dashboards and queries are available to reduce the effort and time to gain insights. It comes with an out-of-the-box dashboard, or users can customize their use of Synack data. Common use cases include: • Security Operations - Integration of vulnerability data into the Security Operations Center (SOC) and related workflows enables security teams to get more efficient and streamline your security stack • Threat Hunting - Find evidence of active or past threats using verified, Synack data about true exploitable vulnerabilities • Incident Management - Efficiently bring incidents to conclusion using all available data sources - Web logs: Correlate exploitable vulnerabilities & locations with web logs to determine if there are other locations where this vulnerability can be exploited - IPS/IDS: Correlate exploitable vulnerabilities & locations with network traffic to define new rules for detection and prevention - Scanners: Correlate exploitable vulnerabilities with scanner data for better scanner efficacy - Threat Intel: Correlate exploitable vulnerabilities & locations with Threat intel to build out predictive patterns • Custom Reporting & Analytics for the above scenarios, or other workflows in your security organization Please login to your Synack Client Portal for configuration options or email Synack support to get started. Further documentation is also available in the Synack Client Portal.

  • Attempts to automatically recover from temporary API errors and rate limiting instead of stopping collection
  • CrowdStrike-branded dashboard styling with light and dark theme support

Bug Fixes

  • Fixed an issue where the add-on could silently fail to authenticate without reporting an error
  • Fixed a crash when selecting SOCKS proxy types in the configuration UI
  • Fixed incorrect API permission instructions shown during input setup

Improvements

  • Inputs now detect network failures and expired credentials with clear error messages
  • Added checkpoint health checks that provide clear guidance if an issue is detected, preventing unnecessary re-collection of data
  • Improved log messages with version info, redacted credentials, and collection progress for faster troubleshooting
  • Updated dashboard panels with corrected queries, proper severity colors, and CrowdStrike branding
  • Updated bundled dependencies including API and platform libraries to their latest supported versions


Description:
This technical add-on is designed to allow CrowdStrike customers to collect and index detections from the CrowdStrike Falcon Platform via the combined alerts v1 API endpoint.

Release Notes:

Update to support Python 3.13, ensuring full compatibility with Splunk Cloud 10.x.


Description:
Gain fast insights and situational awareness around risky infrastructure DomainTools enables Security Operations Centers (SOCs) and security analysts to take domain observables from their network and connect them with other active domains on the Internet. Those connections inform risk assessments, help profile attackers, guide online fraud investigations, and map cyber activity to attacker infrastructure. With the influx in events per second rising, organizations need the ability to execute high-volume queries with improved response times. The DomainTools App for Splunk delivers, with enrichment at scale and drill-down details to add context. Leveraging the DomainTools Iris and Farsight DNSDB datasets, users have immediate access to dozens of attributes attached to every domain event in Splunk, efficiently delivering event enrichment at scale. Domain Monitoring SOCs and Security Analysts can leverage the DomainTools Iris Detect product in Splunk to discover and watch newly registered domains associated with any terms their organization currently monitors (such as a brand or company name), and to monitor domains and append domains to your allowlist (list of trusted domains) from the Domain Investigation workflow. Predictive Risk Scoring DomainTools Risk Score gives teams with emerging threat hunting skills an instant advantage in helping to identify and optionally alert on Splunk events with suspicious domains they would have otherwise missed. Individual component scores give experienced hunters the tools they need to refine their alerts and precisely target their resources. DomainTools Risk Score, including Proximity and Threat Profile classifiers, is available in both key-value stores and Splunk indexes. Proven Capability for Enterprise Organizations DomainTools’ proven solution for Splunk includes a cloud-certified Splunk Application that deploys on Splunk search heads in both standalone and clustered configurations, with and without Splunk Enterprise Security. Event sources can be customized to match the unique requirements of each environment. DomainTools Capabilities in Splunk Reduce MTTD • Bulk enrichment of domains with meaningful context • At-a-glance alerting and reporting of malicious network traffic • Domain monitoring using DomainTools Iris Detect Reduce MTTR • Discover newly registered domains and further enable monitoring • Create a Splunk ES notable event in case a high-risk domain is observed • Investigate connected infrastructure using Iris and Farsight Passive DNS The DomainTools App works in parallel with Splunk Enterprise Security (ES) but does not depend on it. Customers who have not yet deployed ES can still realize significant value from the DomainTools solution.

item.title: AI User Assistent for Splunk - v0.6.0 [New App Release]
item.description:
Platform: Splunk


Release Notes:

Release notes — AI Assistent for Splunk

This file tracks every customer-visible change.

Format: Keep a Changelog. Dates
are ISO-8601. App version in default/app.conf always matches the
top entry.

0.4.0 — 2026-05-18

The "bring your own tools" release. Admins can now define their own LLM
tools — declarative HTTP calls to ServiceNow, internal CMDBs, threat-intel
APIs, etc. — without writing code. The LLM sees them alongside the 23
built-in Splunk tools; the implementation block (URL, auth, headers)
stays server-side so secrets never reach the browser.

Added

  • Custom LLM tools, declarative-HTTP MVP
    (bin/itmip_llm_custom_tools.py).
    Admin-authored JSON definitions mirroring MCP / OpenAI
    function-calling. The { name, description, parameters } triple
    reaches the model; the implementation block (URL, auth,
    credentials, allowed_hosts) is executed on the search head.
  • Implementation types: http (declarative) is shipped.
    splunk_search, kvstore_lookup, python are reserved in the
    schema and rejected at /invoke until 0.5.x.
  • Auth: none / basic / bearer / header — credentials
    resolved server-side from storage/passwords via
    credential_ref. Secrets never appear in the definition or
    cross the browser boundary.
  • Egress safety: per-tool allowed_hosts allowlist, re-checked
    AFTER {{ argName }} template substitution. RFC1918 / loopback
    hosts are refused unless implementation.allow_internal: true.
  • Templating: strict whitelist substitution against the tool
    call's arguments — {{ argName }} only, no Python eval.
  • Response shaping: optional jq or jsonpath transform with
    a max_bytes cap, plus redact_fields for nested key scrubbing
    before the result is sent to the LLM.
  • Guardrails: per-tool rate_limit_per_minute and
    cache_ttl_seconds enforced in-process by splunkd, keyed by
    (user, tool) and (name, argument_hash) respectively.
  • Audit trail: every invocation is logged to a new KVStore
    collection itmip_llm_custom_tool_calls (admin-readable).
  • Admin authoring UI under the Tools tab
    (src/components/CustomToolsSection.tsx)
    with a side-panel editor for the full envelope: identity, scope,
    parameters JSON Schema, HTTP implementation, allowed-hosts tag
    input, auth picker with credential_ref dropdown, jq/jsonpath
    transform expression, guardrails, and an in-UI Save & test
    button that calls /invoke against admin-supplied sample arguments
    and shows the transformed response inline.
  • Import / Export — paste-in / download JSON definitions so MSP
    admins can share definitions across customer environments. Imports
    default to the importing admin's Org/BU; tweak afterwards if you
    need wider scope.
  • Scope model mirrors Splunk's namespace sharing — private
    (owner Org+BU only), app (whole owner Org), global (every
    Org). Reuses the existing tenancy Org/BU model from 0.2.x; no
    new ACL primitive.
  • Frontend tool dispatcher integration
    (src/services/tools.ts). Custom tools
    load at session start, merge with the built-in TOOL_DEFINITIONS,
    go through the per-Org/BU itmip_tool_assignments filter, and
    dispatch via the new /services/itmip_llm/custom_tools/invoke
    endpoint. The LLM cannot tell built-in and custom apart.
  • Schema additions (src/types.ts):
    CustomToolDefinition, CustomToolImplementation,
    CustomToolScope, CustomToolResponse, CustomToolGuardrails
    plus the CustomToolInvokeRequest / CustomToolInvokeResponse
    wire envelope.
  • KVStore collections in
    default/collections.conf:
  • itmip_llm_custom_tools — definitions (admin-write, read-open
    for in-scope users).
  • itmip_llm_custom_tool_calls — audit log (admin-only).
  • Test coverage:
  • tests/python/test_custom_tools.py
    — 20 tests covering definition validation, RFC1918 denial,
    admin-only writes, /invoke happy path, post-substitution
    allowed-hosts re-check, credential_ref resolution, rate-limit
    trip, cache hit, redact_fields, and out-of-scope refusal.
  • tests/playwright/specs/07-custom-tools.spec.ts
    — 4 admin-UI scenarios: section presence, editor surface
    completeness, bad-name refusal, save → list → delete round trip.

Security model (recap)

Custom tools are a powerful primitive — admins can wire the LLM up
to any HTTP API in the organisation. The release is designed so the
blast radius of a mistake or a compromised admin account is bounded:

  • Tool definitions can only be written by admins. End users see them
    in the LLM's tool list but cannot edit.
  • Secrets live in storage/passwords and are resolved server-side
    on every call. The definition can be exported and shared safely —
    the secret stays per-environment.
  • allowed_hosts is a per-tool allowlist enforced after template
    substitution so a parameter-driven URL can't reach an unintended
    host (SSRF defence).
  • RFC1918 and loopback hosts are refused by default — admins must
    set allow_internal: true to wire up internal-network tools.
  • Every invocation is audited with the calling user, the tool, a
    hash of the arguments, the outcome, and the duration.

Example definition

{
  "name": "servicenow_get_incident",
  "version": "1.0.0",
  "title": "Get ServiceNow Incident",
  "description": "Fetches a ServiceNow incident by number (e.g. INC0012345). Use this when the user asks about a specific incident, or when correlating a Splunk alert to an ITSM ticket.",
  "scope": { "sharing": "app", "owner_org": "ACME", "owner_bu": "SECOPS" },
  "parameters": {
    "type": "object",
    "properties": {
      "incident_number": {
        "type": "string",
        "pattern": "^INC[0-9]{7}$",
        "description": "ServiceNow incident number"
      }
    },
    "required": ["incident_number"]
  },
  "implementation": {
    "type": "http",
    "method": "GET",
    "url": "https://acme.service-now.com/api/now/table/incident",
    "query": { "sysparm_query": "number={{ incident_number }}" },
    "auth": { "type": "basic", "credential_ref": "servicenow_readonly", "username": "splunk_ai" },
    "timeout_seconds": 10,
    "allowed_hosts": ["acme.service-now.com"]
  },
  "response": {
    "transform": "jq",
    "expression": ".result[0] | {number, summary: .short_description, state}",
    "max_bytes": 8192
  },
  "guardrails": {
    "rate_limit_per_minute": 30,
    "cache_ttl_seconds": 60,
    "redact_fields": ["sys_id"]
  },
  "enabled": true
}

Upgrade notes

  • No KVStore migration is required. The two new collections start empty.
  • Existing built-in tools are unchanged. Removing a custom tool doesn't
    affect any built-in capability.

0.3.2 — 2026-05-18

The "data-leaving-the-org safety prompt" release. Adds a per-LLM
configurable confirmation overlay so users explicitly acknowledge
before SPL, search results, and Splunk metadata flow to a cloud LLM.

Added

  • Per-LLM security-confirmation modal
    (src/components/SecurityConfirmModal.tsx).
    Full-viewport overlay with a strong, Splunk-Enterprise-specific
    warning that lists every class of data the LLM may receive
    (question text, SPL the LLM tests, event rows / lookups / dashboard
    panel data from tools the LLM calls, knowledge-object payloads,
    Splunk metadata like index/sourcetype/host/user/role/app names).
    Two buttons: "I understand — send" + "Cancel". Esc dismisses.
  • Trigger model:
  • Fires on first Ask with each LLM in a browser session.
  • Fires on LLM switch — switching from an internal LLM to
    Anthropic / OpenAI / etc. re-prompts because it's a different
    external connection.
  • Acknowledgement is per-LlmConfig._key, per-session.
  • Full page reload re-prompts; the Ask-tab Clear button does NOT
    reset.
  • Settings UI in the LLM-config modal:
  • New checkbox "Show security confirmation before sending",
    default checked for new configs and for the bootstrap
    Anthropic row.
  • Optional "Custom warning message" textarea revealed when the
    checkbox is on. Placeholders the modal substitutes:
    {provider}, {endpoint_host}, {call_mode}.
  • Schema (src/types.ts): two new optional fields
    on LlmConfig: confirm_external: boolean and
    confirm_external_message: string. Loader treats a missing
    confirm_external as true so installs upgrading from 0.3.1
    inherit the safety prompt without any KVStore migration.
  • Playwright coverage — new
    tests/playwright/specs/06-security-confirm.spec.ts
    with four scenarios: modal appears on first paint, Accept dismisses
  • reveals the Ask UI, Cancel dismisses + keeps the LLM selected,
    Settings exposes the checkbox + custom-text textarea.

Changed

  • The bootstrap Anthropic config (
    DFLT_DFLT_anthropic_central) now ships with confirm_external: true — first-time users see the modal explaining what's about to
    leave their environment.
  • Playwright helper openAssistant accepts a
    { dismissSecurityConfirm: false } option for specs that want to
    assert on the overlay rather than dismiss it. Default behaviour
    dismisses so existing specs work unchanged.
  • App version 0.3.1 → 0.3.2.

Default warning text

The default copy is deliberately specific:

You are about to send a request to {provider} at {endpoint_host} —
a third-party Large Language Model service outside your
organisation's Splunk Enterprise boundary. Once dispatched, the
following information MAY be transmitted to that service: your
question text verbatim; Splunk knowledge-object payloads the LLM
examines or creates (saved-search SPL, dashboard XML, alert
configuration, lookup contents, macro definitions); search-result
rows from any Splunk tool the LLM invokes (events, lookup samples,
dashboard-panel previews, saved-search output); Splunk metadata it
discovers along the way (index names, sourcetypes, host names, user
names, role names, app names, AI-Toolkit model names); SPL
fragments the LLM generates and tests against your data while
reasoning. — Before continuing, confirm: (1) no production
credentials, API tokens, customer PII, or restricted data; (2)
sensitive values masked; (3) your organisation's policy permits
{provider}; (4) the network path ({call_mode}) is acceptable.

Verification

  • TypeScript clean. Webpack clean → main.js 589 KB.
  • 27 / 27 Playwright tests pass (4 new + 23 existing).
  • 48 / 48 Python tests pass (no Python-side change in this release).

0.3.1 — 2026-05-15

The "make MLTK models work for non-admin users" release. Fixes an
end-to-end gap where AI-Toolkit templates run from any app other than
Splunk_ML_Toolkit produced dashboards that failed with "Model does not
exist".

Added

  • Privileged MLTK model-share endpoint
    /services/itmip_llm/mltk_share     (bin/itmip_llm_mltk_share.py).
    Promotes AI-Assistent-trained model lookup-table-files to
    owner=nobody, sharing=global using splunkd's system token. Works
    for any authenticated user — no admin_all_objects capability
    required. Scope-limited via:
  • Regex pin on model name: ^mltk_[a-z]+_[a-z0-9_]+_aiasst_v\d+$.
  • App allow-list (user must see the app; system apps denied).
  • Per-user rate limit (10 promotions / minute).
  • Audit log line on every successful share + KVStore registry row.
  • itmip_llm_mltk_models KVStore audit registry. One row per
    shared model with model_name, host_app, created_by,
    created_at_epoch, template, description, last_shared_at.
    Admins audit with | inputlookup itmip_llm_mltk_models.
  • aiasst model-naming convention. Every model the assistant
    trains is mltk_<algo>_<thing>_aiasst_v<N> — visible in the
    AI Toolkit's Models tab so admins can tell at a glance which models
    came from the AI Assistent.
  • "Auditing AI-Assistent-created MLTK models" section added to
    docs/ADMIN_MANUAL.md with SPL recipes for
    listing, tailing the audit log, and cleanup.
  • tests/python/test_mltk_share.py — unit tests covering: regex
    pin, app allow-list, rate limiter, happy-path promotion, 404 on
    missing files, registry upsert.

Changed

  • splunk_share_mltk_model_globally tool now POSTs to the new
    /services/itmip_llm/mltk_share endpoint instead of calling
    Splunk's ACL endpoint directly with the caller's session token.
    Same tool surface for the LLM — the implementation just moved
    server-side. Works for user / power roles for the first time.
  • All 5 AI-Toolkit templates updated:
  • Model names switched to the new aiasst convention.
  • Training and scoring saved searches stay in the calling app
    (no more target_app="Splunk_ML_Toolkit").
  • Saved-search descriptions auto-populated with "Generated by AI
    Assistent for Splunk. <algorithm> on <field>." so admins can audit.
  • Clustering template now correctly instructs sharing of BOTH the
    scaler and kmeans models.
  • docs/USER_MANUAL.md gained an "AI Toolkit models you create
    via this app" section explaining the aiasst naming + that no
    admin role is needed.

Fixed

  • Dashboards generated from AI-Toolkit templates running outside the
    Splunk_ML_Toolkit app threw "Failed to load model — Model does not
    exist".     Root cause: fit … into <model> writes the model file
    into the calling app's lookups directory at default app sharing,
    not global. The new mltk_share endpoint promotes it so apply <name> resolves from any app.

Security

  • New finding MLT1 added to
    docs/SECURITY_AUDIT.md — documents the
    privilege-elevation design, the mitigations (regex pin, app
    allow-list, rate limit, audit trail), and the accepted residual
    risk (users can globally share their own AI-Assistent-trained
    models; not the model's source data).

0.3.0 — 2026-05-14

The "make it commercial" release. Adds licensing, multi-tenancy
enforcement, corporate-IAM integration, role-specific user guides, and
a re-audited security baseline. Builds cleanly through Splunk
AppInspect.

Added

  • Cryptolens licensing end-to-end. Admin-only License tab in
    the Web UI activates a 25-character key, validates against
    Cryptolens, removes a stored licence, and manages expiry-warning
    email recipients. Browser-direct activation flow works on air-gapped
    Search Heads — the SH never has to reach the licensing vendor.
  • Five licence tiers:
  • Personal (free, no key required): 1 Org, 1 BU, 1 concurrent ask
    session, no History, no Tokens & Costs.
  • Professional: 1 Org, 3 BUs, full features. Node-locked.
  • Enterprise: 1 Org, unlimited BUs. Node-locked.
  • MSP: unlimited Orgs + BUs. One key activates against multiple
    Splunk environments     up to the vendor-set machine cap.
  • PoV (time-limited) and NFR (Not-for-Resale, MSP features, 1
    year, no node lock) variants supported. Both render a badge next
    to the app title.
  • Tier-aware caps on Orgs & BUs. UI disables + Add Org and
    + BU at cap; server-side enforcement at
    /services/itmip_llm/tenancy (new persistent REST handler) is the
    authoritative boundary. Admins who bypass via raw KVStore still hit
    no soft error today, but the UI / API surface is consistent.
  • Customer authorisation hook. Drop a Python file at
    local/bin/customer_authorisation.py and the Splunk-side proxy
    invokes it before every outbound LLM request to mint fresh headers
    from a corporate IAM gateway (WebEAM.Next, Ping, Okta, AzureAD,
    internal SAML…). Documented per-LLM toggle in the Settings UI.
  • License-expiry alert auto-creation. Saving recipient emails on
    the License tab creates a Splunk Enterprise saved alert
    (itmip_llm_license_expiry_warning) that fires when the licence is
    within 30 days of expiring. Scripted input
    bin/itmip_llm_license_monitor.py runs every 6 h and is silent
    until the threshold is crossed.
  • AI Toolkit model-namespace handling. The 5 MLTK templates
    (outlier, multi-field anomaly, forecasting, clustering, prediction)
    now write their training and scoring saved searches into
    Splunk_ML_Toolkit with global sharing, then call the new
    splunk_share_mltk_model_globally tool so dashboards / alerts in any
    app can apply <model> cleanly. Companion dashboards still live in
    the user's current app.
  • New LLM tools:
  • splunk_create_saved_search / splunk_update_saved_search gained
    target_app and target_sharing parameters.
  • splunk_share_mltk_model_globally — promotes a
    __mlspl_<name>.{csv,mlmodel,onnx} lookup-table-file to
    owner=nobody, sharing=global, app=Splunk_ML_Toolkit.
  • Role-specific manuals version-stamped 0.3.0:
  • docs/installation_instructions.md — fresh-install walkthrough.
  • docs/USER_MANUAL.md — for end users.
  • docs/ADMIN_MANUAL.md — for admin / sc_admin.
  • Playwright web-UI test suite (tests/playwright/): 23 specs
    covering app boot, role-gating, template editor, LLM config modal,
    License tab visibility + content, customer auth hook checkbox. CI
    friendly; runnable locally with npx playwright test.
  • Python unit tests for the customer-auth invoker, licence tier
    resolver, GUID resolver, and tenancy cap enforcer (33 tests total).

Changed

  • App label renamed in default/app.conf to "AI Assistent for
    Splunk".
  • All 27 use-case templates now ship as status = operational
    (previously 21 were draft and admin-only on the Ask tab). Existing
    installs auto-promote on first page-load after upgrade via the
    refreshSystemEntry loop.
  • Bootstrap Anthropic LLM (DFLT_DFLT_anthropic_central)
    defaults to call_mode = splunk_proxy so the central key never
    reaches the browser. Users with the bootstrap config don't need
    their own key once an admin stores the central one.
  • Tokens & Costs event sourcetype + cost-estimator pull per-model
    pricing from src/services/llm/providers.ts. Cost numbers now
    reflect the actual model the user picked, not a fixed Sonnet rate.
  • SplunkApiError.message now surfaces the server-side error
    body verbatim (e.g. "License 'professional' allows up to 3 BU(s)
    per Org; 'ACME' already has 3."    ) so the UI shows actionable copy
    instead of generic 4xx text.
  • Security audit doc (docs/SECURITY_AUDIT.md)
    rewritten as a status board: every prior BLOCKER / HIGH is marked
    RESOLVED with the iteration that fixed it; new findings from
    customer-auth hook / licensing / tenancy wrapper added.
  • docs/FUNCTIONALITY.md updated with a "What's new in 0.3.0"
    section and cross-links to the new manuals.

Fixed

  • License-expiry saved alert was created but never sent email.
    Splunk Enterprise 9.x needs both actions = email (to enable the
    action) and action.email.* parameters (to configure it); only the
    latter was being written. The alert now lights up the "Send email"
    trigger action in the UI.
  • License-expiry alert SPL had no index=. Switched to a new
    ai_assistant_license_index macro that resolves to
    index=main sourcetype=itmip_llm_license by default and can be
    overridden in local/macros.conf to route into a dedicated index.
  • Removing every recipient email left a dead alert behind. Now
    saving an empty recipient list deletes the saved alert outright
    instead of leaving one that fires and emails no one.
  • make spl packaging deleted the React bundle after it finished
    archiving (a side effect of force-adding appserver/static/build/
    on a temp branch + git checkout - to the original branch). The
    Makefile now re-runs npm run build at the very end so the local
    Splunk install stays in a runnable state after every packaging run.
  • Makefile was being shipped in the .spl, tripping AppInspect's
    check_destructive_commands on its dev-cleanup rm -rf
    instructions. Added Makefile export-ignore to .gitattributes
    and switched git archive to --worktree-attributes so the
    exclusion takes effect without needing a commit first.
  • AI Toolkit dashboards generated from outside the Splunk_ML_Toolkit
    app threw "Failed to load model — Model does not exist".     The
    template flow now pins the training + scoring saved searches to
    Splunk_ML_Toolkit + global sharing, then explicitly promotes the
    model file so apply resolves from any calling app.
  • MIME-type / 404 errors at the React shell when
    appserver/static/build/main.js was missing post-rename or
    post-make spl. Documented in
    tasks/lessons.md and now self-healing via the
    Makefile fix above.
  • CSRF silent fallback in splunkFetch removed — state-changing
    requests now throw a clear SplunkApiError(status=0) when the
    token cookie is missing, instead of degrading to an unauthenticated
    request that splunkd will reject far downstream.

Security

  • All 5 BLOCKER + 9 HIGH findings from the v0.2.x audit are
    resolved.     Highlights:
  • /services/itmip_llm/secret POST/DELETE now requires admin
    server-side; GET is rate-limited and gated on per-LLM allow-list.
  • /services/itmip_llm/proxy no longer accepts caller-supplied
    endpoint; uses the stored LlmConfig.endpoint. Caller-supplied
    extra_headers filtered against a 3-entry allow-list.
  • /services/itmip_llm/api_key admin-only; bootstrap LLM defaults
    to splunk_proxy so the key stays on the SH.
  • KVStore collection ACLs for itmip_llm_configs,
    itmip_organisations, itmip_business_units,
    itmip_tool_assignments, itmip_llm_license tightened to
    read/write: [admin, power / sc_admin].
  • SPL injection guard: rejectSideEffectSpl() runs inside every
    LLM-dispatched search and refuses outputlookup, outputcsv,
    sendemail, sendalert, collect, summaryindex, tscollect,
    metasearch, script, runshellscript, delete.
  • Dashboard XML lint refuses <script>, <iframe>, <object>,
    <embed>, javascript: URLs, inline event handlers.
  • Per-user rate limits added to the most-spammable endpoints (30/min
    on secret GET + proxy, 120/min on usage_log).
  • The full status board is in docs/SECURITY_AUDIT.md.

Removed

  • Legacy v0.1 "Anthropic API key" card under Settings. The
    storage path (storage/passwords realm = itmip_ai_splunk_assistent_app,
    name = anthropic_api_key) is still read transparently by
    loadSecretForConfig() as a fallback for the bootstrap LLM, so
    existing installs that pre-date the rename keep working.

Known limitations

  • Concurrent-session enforcement on the Personal tier is UI-only —
    cross-browser hard enforcement needs a heartbeat protocol.
  • The Cryptolens product access token is embedded in code (this is
    the vendor-recommended pattern — it is the product's read-only
    API key, not a customer secret). A scanner may flag it; document
    the rationale on Splunkbase submission if asked.

0.2.x — internal release stream

A series of internal iterations between 2026-03 and 2026-05-12 leading
up to 0.3.0. Highlights worth knowing if you're upgrading from a
pre-0.3.0 build:

Added (during 0.2.x)

  • Multi-LLM support: Anthropic, OpenAI, Azure OpenAI, Groq, Gemini,
    Bedrock, Ollama, OpenRouter. Pick provider + model per LLM
    configuration.
  • Two call modes per LLM: browser_direct (lowest latency,
    CORS-limited) and splunk_proxy (works everywhere, keys
    server-side).
  • Streaming responses for Anthropic and OpenAI-compatible providers.
  • Multi-tenant Organisations + Business Units. Templates and LLM
    configs scope per Org/BU. Resolved per page load from the user's
    Splunk app + role.
  • Use-case templates for SPL searches, Simple XML dashboards,
    Dashboard Studio JSON, alerts (with companion dashboards), saved
    searches, reports, lookups, field extractions, plus 10 Splunk AI
    Toolkit pipelines.
  • Tokens & Costs tab — multi-axis side-by-side cost analytics
    (App / User / Model / Provider / Org / BU / LLM config) over time.
  • Tools tab — per-Org/BU enable/disable of every LLM tool.
  • TLS CA certificate (PEM) upload per LLM (server-side proxy
    honours customer-internal CAs).
  • Extra HTTP headers per LLM (static tokens, customer-internal
    gateway headers).
  • KVStore-backed user history with per-question template / LLM /
    provider / model / token / cost attribution and clickable links to
    every created knowledge object.

Renamed (during 0.2.x)

  • App id stayed itmip_ai_splunk_assistent_app; label evolved from
    "Claude Assistant for Splunk" → "AI User Assistent for Splunk" →
    (in 0.3.0) "AI Assistent for Splunk".
  • All bin/itmip_claude_*.py Python handlers renamed to
    bin/itmip_llm_*.py. Legacy URLs (/services/itmip_claude/*)
    retired; new ones live under /services/itmip_llm/*.

0.1.x — pre-history

The original "Claude Assistant for Splunk" with a single Anthropic
provider and a hand-stored API key under storage/passwords realm =
itmip_ai_splunk_assistent_app, name = anthropic_api_key. The
legacy key path is still readable by the bootstrap LLM in 0.3.x for
backward compatibility — no migration step needed.

Support for IPGeolocation.io v3 APIs

The app has been upgraded to target the latest IPGeolocation.io v3 APIs and database services.

  • company object
  • asn object

Updated ipsecurity and ipsecuritybatch Commands

  • ipsecurity now accepts only the ip parameter.
  • ipsecuritybatch now accepts only the ips parameter.
  • All previously supported optional parameters have been removed.

Advanced Database Bundle

IP To City, Company, ASN, Abuse, and Security

  • Company information
  • ASN details
  • Abuse intelligence
  • Security and threat insights

API Plan Support

Developer Plan

Paid Plans

  • Supports higher lookup volumes and production workloads.
  • Additional details are available on the official pricing page.

Improvements

  • Enhanced compatibility with the latest IPGeolocation.io platform architecture.
  • Better alignment with official v3 API standards and documentation.

Compatibility Notes

Users upgrading from previous versions should review command parameter changes, especially for:

  • ipgeolocation
  • ipgeolocationbatch
  • ipsecurity
  • ipsecuritybatch

Deprecated parameters used in older API versions are no longer supported in v3.

Recommendation

  • Expanded database coverage
  • Native v3 API compatibility
  • Access to free-tier lookups
  • Enhanced security and abuse intelligence

item.description:

Release Notes:

v1.2.3 (2026-05-11)

Critical Fix — SSL/TLS Runtime Crash

Fixed a fatal SSL_CERTIFICATE_VERIFY_FAILED exception that prevented all data collection on Splunk Enterprise deployments using the default self-signed management certificate.

Root Cause: The internal REST API call to splunkd (127.0.0.1:8089) was configured with verify=True. Since splunkd uses a self-signed certificate by default, every input execution cycle crashed before reaching the Elasticsearch cluster.

Resolution: Reverted to verify=False for the localhost-only REST call. Session-key authentication provides sufficient security for this internal request.

Impact: All users on v1.2.2 are affected and should upgrade immediately.

Added — Comprehensive Operational Logging

7 structured log points covering the entire data collection cycle:

  • Input Config: cluster target, ES index, date field, polling interval
  • Filter Config: ENABLED/DISABLED status with key/value parameters
  • Proxy Status: ENABLED with host/port, or NOT configured
  • Sourcetype: CUSTOM or DEFAULT resolution
  • ES Client: hosts count, retries, timeout, sniffing, TLS verification
  • Query DSL: full Elasticsearch query body logged before execution
  • Response Summary: total_hits, first page doc count, scroll_id

All logs are written to index=_internal — operators can now diagnose collection issues without inspecting Python source code.

Added — Internal Log Monitoring Resilience

  • Added explicit [monitor://...] stanza with crcSalt=<SOURCE> to prevent fishbucket CRC corruption after Deployment Server push events or log file rotation.
  • Added props.conf and transforms.conf for structured parsing and index-time field extraction of operational logs.
  • 20 index-time field extractions for operational and audit events.

Inherited from v1.2.2

  • python.required = 3.9, 3.13 for Splunk 10.2+ (Python 3.13) dual compatibility
  • All security hardening from v1.2.1 (SSRF protection, input sanitization)

Upgrade: Drop-in replacement for v1.2.2. No configuration changes required.

Compatibility: Splunk Enterprise 9.4, 10.0, 10.1, 10.2

Requires: Elasticsearch 8.x

Libraries: elasticsearch-py 8.19.3, elastic-transport 8.17.1

Features multi-cluster profiles, DSL query filters, scroll-based pagination with crash recovery, document-level deduplication, SSL/TLS support, and a full GUI configuration experience. Platform: Splunk


Release Notes:

# Release Notes: AWS-DFD-Visualizer v2.5.19 (Cumulative Update)

**Release Date:** May 10, 2026

**Framework:** Splunk Unified Dashboard Framework (Dashboard Studio) & Classic SimpleXML

## Overview

Version 2.5.19 is a major cumulative update (rolling up hotfixes 2.5.9 through 2.5.19) that completely hardens the React/D3 migration for Splunk Dashboard Studio. It resolves multiple critical rendering bugs, theme detection failures, and SPL parsing edge-cases, ensuring production-ready stability for both Dark Mode NOC dashboards and Classic SimpleXML layouts.

## Engineering Improvements

* **Cypress Component Testing:** We have fully decoupled the React rendering layer from Splunk UI dependencies, enabling a robust Cypress headless testing pipeline. Node physics (D3) and mathematical coordinate mapping are now automatically verified before `.spl` compilation, eliminating manual "upload-and-pray" cycles.

* **Theme Hook & AMD Module Removal:** Ripped out failing `@splunk/themes` dependencies that caused silent React unmounts (White Screen of Death) and resolved the AMD `CustomVizClassDef is not a constructor` wrapper issue natively at the Webpack layer via `libraryExport: 'default'`.

## Bug Fixes

* **White Box Render Bug in Dashboard Studio:** The visualizer now features robust dark mode detection tailored for Dashboard Studio. It intercepts `$config` payloads to correctly trigger dark themes when `"backgroundColor": "#000000"` is detected, and forces the container background to `transparent` so it seamlessly inherits the exact Splunk dashboard panel color behind it.

* **SPL Column Fallback Parsing Error:** Fixed an issue where queries lacking a specific `node_label` field incorrectly fell back to the 4th column (`edge_label`), mislabeling nodes with connection protocols (e.g., "HTTPS" instead of "Internet").

* **D3 Physics Engine NaN Collapse:** Fixed a catastrophic division-by-zero math cascade in D3's `forceCollide` algorithm. Nodes now instantiate with a random spatial jitter algorithm (`Math.random() * 50 - 25`), preventing perfectly stacked coordinates from crashing the SVG renderer.

* **Dashboard Studio Results Support:** Added fallback support to process object arrays (`data.results`) natively passed by Dashboard Studio instead of forcing Classic SimpleXML row arrays (`data.rows`).

* **SVG Coordinate Scaling:** Added an explicit `viewBox\="0 0 1200 1000"` and a hardcoded `minHeight: 400px` to decouple the visualization from Splunk's bounding box logic, forcing the map to scale dynamically into any panel size without clipping.


Short Description:
Interactive D3.js force-directed graph for AWS Security Data Flows, featuring official AWS icons and Application Composer aesthetics for "Zero Trust" visibility.

The AWS DFD Visualizer provides a high-fidelity, interactive force-directed graph visualization specifically designed for AWS infrastructure and security data flows. It allows users to instantly identify connectivity patterns, data silos, and security relationships across services like Lambda, S3, RDS, and CloudWatch.
